## Overview

We assess the sensitivity of the dynamic eQTL functional classifications (Early,
Middle, Late, and Switch) to the evaluation-grid step size and the number of
posterior Monte Carlo draws. The main analysis uses evaluation-grid step `0.10`
on $[0, 15]$ and $M = 3{,}000$ posterior draws. Here we compare the resulting
`lfsr` values for the discovered gene--variant pairs in each category against
alternative grid steps (`0.15` and `0.05` at $M = 3{,}000$) and alternative
Monte Carlo sample sizes ($M = 2{,}000$ and $M = 5{,}000$ at grid step `0.10`).

For posterior trajectory draw $\beta^{(m)}(t)$, the four functional statistics are

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{\mathrm{early}}^{(m)}
&= \sup_{t\leq3}|\beta^{(m)}(t)|-\sup_{t>3}|\beta^{(m)}(t)|,\\
T_{\mathrm{middle}}^{(m)}
&= \sup_{3<t<12}|\beta^{(m)}(t)|
   -\sup_{t\leq3\;\mathrm{or}\;t\geq12}|\beta^{(m)}(t)|,\\
T_{\mathrm{late}}^{(m)}
&= \sup_{t\geq12}|\beta^{(m)}(t)|-\sup_{t<12}|\beta^{(m)}(t)|,\\
T_{\mathrm{switch}}^{(m)}
&= \min\!\left\{\sup_t \beta^{(m)}(t),-\inf_t \beta^{(m)}(t)\right\}-0.25,
\end{aligned}
$$

and the local false sign rate for category $c$ is estimated by

$$
\widehat{\mathrm{lfsr}}_c
=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}I\!\left\{T_c^{(m)}\leq0\right\}.
$$

```{r analysis-population-table}
category_display_names <- c(
  early = "Early",
  middle = "Middle",
  late = "Late",
  switch = "Switch"
)

population_table <- data.frame(
  Category = unname(category_display_names[population_summary$category]),
  Definition = c(
    "Strongest effect during the first three days (t <= 3)",
    "Strongest effect in the middle window (3 < t < 12)",
    "Strongest effect during the last four days (t >= 12)",
    "Positive and negative excursions both exceed 0.25"
  ),
  `Discovered pairs` = population_summary$n_pairs,
  `Unique genes` = population_summary$n_genes,
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  population_table,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Table 1. Dynamic eQTL functional categories and numbers of discovered pairs and genes (cumulative FSR <= 0.05 at grid step 0.10 and 3,000 posterior draws)."
)
```

```{r scatter-construction}
library(ggplot2)

build_comparison_data <- function(comparison_id) {
  comparison_spec <- configuration$comparisons[
    configuration$comparisons$comparison_id == comparison_id,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(comparison_spec) != 1L) {
    stop("The requested comparison is not uniquely specified.")
  }

  x_rows <- pair_lfsr[
    pair_lfsr$setting_id == comparison_spec$x_setting_id,
    c("category", "pair_id", "gene_symbol", "lfsr"),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  y_rows <- pair_lfsr[
    pair_lfsr$setting_id == comparison_spec$y_setting_id,
    c("category", "pair_id", "lfsr"),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  names(x_rows)[names(x_rows) == "lfsr"] <- "x_lfsr"
  names(y_rows)[names(y_rows) == "lfsr"] <- "y_lfsr"

  plot_data <- merge(
    x_rows,
    y_rows,
    by = c("category", "pair_id"),
    all = FALSE,
    sort = FALSE
  )

  plot_data$category_panel <- factor(
    plot_data$category,
    levels = category_order,
    labels = unname(category_display_names[category_order])
  )
  plot_data
}

build_comparison_plot <- function(comparison_id, x_label, y_label) {
  plot_data <- build_comparison_data(comparison_id)

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = x_lfsr, y = y_lfsr)) +
    geom_abline(
      intercept = c(-0.01, 0.01),
      slope = 1,
      color = "grey65",
      linewidth = 0.45,
      linetype = "dotted"
    ) +
    geom_abline(
      intercept = 0,
      slope = 1,
      color = "grey20",
      linewidth = 0.55
    ) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0.05,
      color = "grey72",
      linewidth = 0.4,
      linetype = "dashed"
    ) +
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = 0.05,
      color = "grey72",
      linewidth = 0.4,
      linetype = "dashed"
    ) +
    geom_point(
      color = "#1B9E77",
      alpha = 0.65,
      size = 1.4
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~category_panel, ncol = 2) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 0.13),
      breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.10),
      labels = c("0", "0.05", "0.10"),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.02))
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 0.13),
      breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.10),
      labels = c("0", "0.05", "0.10"),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.02))
    ) +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey92", linewidth = 0.35),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.0, "lines")
    )
}
```

## Evaluation-grid sensitivity

We first compare evaluation-grid step `0.10` against a coarser grid (`0.15`) and
a finer grid (`0.05`), holding the number of posterior draws fixed at $M = 3{,}000$.
In all plots below, the solid diagonal indicates equality and the dotted lines
mark an absolute `lfsr` difference of `0.01`.

```{r grid-0p10-vs-0p05, fig.cap="Figure 1. Evaluation-grid sensitivity: step 0.10 versus 0.05 at 3,000 posterior draws across the four functional categories."}
build_comparison_plot(
  comparison_id = "grid_0p10_vs_0p05_M3000",
  x_label = "lfsr at grid step 0.10",
  y_label = "lfsr at grid step 0.05"
)
```

```{r grid-0p10-vs-0p15, fig.cap="Figure 2. Evaluation-grid sensitivity: step 0.10 versus 0.15 at 3,000 posterior draws across the four functional categories."}
build_comparison_plot(
  comparison_id = "grid_0p10_vs_0p15_M3000",
  x_label = "lfsr at grid step 0.10",
  y_label = "lfsr at grid step 0.15"
)
```

Across the four categories, mean absolute `lfsr` differences relative to step
`0.10` range from `0.0003` to `0.0016` for step `0.05` and from `0.0005` to
`0.0016` for step `0.15`, with every pair differing by at most `0.01`.

## Posterior Monte Carlo sensitivity

Next, we compare $M = 3{,}000$ posterior draws against $M = 5{,}000$ and
$M = 2{,}000$ draws at evaluation-grid step `0.10`.

```{r M3000-vs-M5000, fig.cap="Figure 3. Posterior Monte Carlo sensitivity: 3,000 versus 5,000 posterior draws at evaluation-grid step 0.10."}
build_comparison_plot(
  comparison_id = "M3000_vs_M5000_grid_0p10",
  x_label = "lfsr with 3,000 draws",
  y_label = "lfsr with 5,000 draws"
)
```

```{r M2000-vs-M3000, fig.cap="Figure 4. Posterior Monte Carlo sensitivity: 2,000 versus 3,000 posterior draws at evaluation-grid step 0.10."}
build_comparison_plot(
  comparison_id = "M2000_vs_M3000_grid_0p10",
  x_label = "lfsr with 2,000 draws",
  y_label = "lfsr with 3,000 draws"
)
```

Across categories, mean absolute `lfsr` differences are `0.0017`--`0.0023`
between 3,000 and 5,000 draws (with more than 99.8% of pairs differing by at
most `0.01`) and `0.0020`--`0.0022` between 2,000 and 3,000 draws.

## Reproducibility

The sensitivity analysis can be reproduced with:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
Rscript --vanilla \
  code/revision_simulations/internal/evaluation_grid_sensitivity/run_all_category_baseline_discovery_sensitivity.R \
  --num-cores 2 \
  --seed 20260826 \
  --middle-definition open_3_12 \
  --output-id evaluation_grid_mc_all_category_current_fashr0143_20260826
```
